prompts.common:
You are an engineering assistant correcting a mechanical part.

Part: a solid rectangular drip tray, 190 mm x 135 mm x H mm (H is the height you
control). Material ABS-like: E = 2200 MPa, nu = 0.35. Linear static case: the tray
is fixed along one long edge band and carries a 100 N downward load on the
opposite edge band.

Requirement: the maximum displacement must be at most T mm (value given below).
The current design at height H0 FAILS this requirement. Increasing the height
stiffens the tray. The allowed height domain is [20, 31] mm — any proposal
outside it is rejected without measurement.

Respond ONLY through the structured output with your proposed height in mm.
prompts.l0Example:
You are an engineering assistant correcting a mechanical part.

Part: a solid rectangular drip tray, 190 mm x 135 mm x H mm (H is the height you
control). Material ABS-like: E = 2200 MPa, nu = 0.35. Linear static case: the tray
is fixed along one long edge band and carries a 100 N downward load on the
opposite edge band.

Requirement: the maximum displacement must be at most T mm (value given below).
The current design at height H0 FAILS this requirement. Increasing the height
stiffens the tray. The allowed height domain is [20, 31] mm — any proposal
outside it is rejected without measurement.

Respond ONLY through the structured output with your proposed height in mm.

T = 0.088 mm. H0 = 29 mm (fails).

You get NO simulation feedback. Propose, in one shot, the height most likely to
satisfy the requirement with minimal oversizing. One single real FEA solve will
then judge your proposal.

proposals.rationale: Cantilever plate: δ ∝ 1/H³. Since H0=29 mm barely fails T=0.088 mm, scaling by (H_new/29)³ = δ_29/0.088 with an assumed small margin above 0.088 gives H_new ≈ 29.7 mm. Rounding up to 30 mm stays within [20,31] and provides the minimum stiffness gain (~9.6% displacement reduction) needed to cross the threshold without unnecessary oversizing.

Cantilever bending stiffness scales as H³. Moving from 29 to 30 mm multiplies stiffness by (30/29)³ ≈ 1.107, reducing displacement by ~9.7%. If the 29 mm failure is marginal (δ just above 0.088 mm), 30 mm lands safely below the threshold while avoiding unnecessary oversizing versus the 31 mm ceiling.

Cantilever plate stiffness scales as H³. Going from 29 mm to 30 mm gives a stiffness ratio of (30/29)³ ≈ 1.107, reducing displacement by ~9%. This is the minimum increment that provides a meaningful margin over the failing design while avoiding unnecessary oversizing; 31 mm is held in reserve if the current displacement is more than ~20% above the 0.088 mm limit.

Cantilever plate model: displacement scales as 1/H³. At H0=28 mm the displacement δ₀ > 0.092 mm. Using δ ∝ PL³/(E·b·H³/12), δ at 28 mm ≈ 0.107 mm. To reach T=0.092 mm: H = 28·(0.107/0.092)^(1/3) ≈ 29.5 mm. Rounding up to 30 mm gives a small safety margin while staying well within [20,31] and avoiding oversizing.

For a plate in bending, stiffness scales as H³. The displacement ratio is (H0/H)³. At H0=28 mm the tray fails; a step to 30 mm gives a stiffness multiplier of (30/28)³ ≈ 1.23, reducing displacement by ~19 %. That headroom is enough to clear a threshold that is just above the H0 value, while staying well inside the [20, 31] mm domain and avoiding the hard ceiling at 31 mm.

Plate-strip cantilever model: δ = 4·q·L³·(1−ν²)/(E·h³), q=100/190 N/mm, L=135 mm, E=2200 MPa, ν=0.35. At H=28 mm: δ≈0.094 mm (fails T=0.092). Required crossing at H≈28.2 mm. Proposing H=29 mm gives δ≈0.085 mm, ~8 % margin over T while staying close to the minimum. Domain check: 29 ∈ [20,31].

Cantilever plate analogy: δ ∝ PL³/(3EI) with I = b·H³/12. At H=27 mm the model fails. Scaling: H_new = H0·(δ0/T)^(1/3). Estimating δ0 ≈ 0.120 mm at H0=27 gives H_new ≈ 27·(0.120/0.095)^(1/3) ≈ 29.1 mm. H=29 is borderline (≈0.097 mm by the same scaling); H=30 gives ≈0.087 mm, safely under 0.095 mm with minimal oversizing, and stays within [20,31].

Plate bending model: δ = PL³/(3bD), D = EH³/[12(1−ν²)]. With P=100 N, L=135 mm, b=190 mm, E=2200 MPa, ν=0.35 → D_factor = 10.53. At H0=27 mm, δ ≈ 0.105 mm (fails). The threshold H satisfies H³ ≥ 21 746 mm³, giving H ≈ 27.9 mm. H=28 mm lands at ~0.094 mm — within tolerance but within model error. H=29 mm gives δ ≈ 0.085 mm, a safe 10 % margin without oversizing beyond the next integer step.

Bending stiffness scales as H³. At H0=27 mm the tray fails, meaning displacement d(27) > 0.095 mm. Assuming d(27) ≈ 0.11 mm (a modest overrun), the required height is 27 × (0.11/0.095)^(1/3) ≈ 28.4 mm. Rounding up to 29 mm gives a safe margin while staying well within the [20, 31] mm domain and avoiding unnecessary oversizing.

Plate bending stiffness scales as h³. At H0=25 mm the tray fails δ≤0.1 mm. Targeting h=30 mm gives a stiffness ratio of (30/25)³ ≈ 1.73, which should bring a moderately failing design (δ₀ up to ~0.17 mm) within tolerance while staying 1 mm below the domain ceiling, leaving headroom if the first solve still misses.

Bending stiffness scales as H^3. Going from 25 mm to 30 mm multiplies stiffness by (30/25)^3 ≈ 1.73, so displacement drops to roughly 58 % of the failing value. Without knowing the exact failure margin this factor gives comfortable headroom while staying 1 mm below the 31 mm ceiling, avoiding the boundary risk.

Cantilever plate bending: δ ∝ 1/t³. Rough estimate at H0=25 mm gives δ ≈ 0.15 mm (100N × 135³ / (3 × 2200 × 190×25³/12)). To reach T=0.1 mm, need (25/H)³ = 0.1/0.15 → H ≈ 28.7 mm. Rounding up to 29 mm stays well inside [20,31] and provides a small safety margin without over-stiffening.

Plate bending stiffness scales as H³. At H0=23 mm the tray fails; target T=0.11 mm. Without knowing the exact over-shoot, a conservative mid-range correction H=28 mm yields a stiffness ratio of (28/23)³ ≈ 1.81×, enough to cover a ~40-80 % excess displacement while staying well inside [20,31] and avoiding unnecessary oversizing.

Cantilever plate model (fixed long edge, load on opposite long edge): D = E·H³/[12(1−ν²)] = 208.9·H³ N·mm. Max tip deflection δ = (P/b)·L³/(3D) = 2067/H³ mm, with L=135 mm span, b=190 mm, P=100 N. At H0=23: δ≈0.170 mm (fails). Requirement δ≤0.11 gives H≥(2067/0.11)^(1/3)≈26.6 mm. H=27 mm yields δ≈0.105 mm, just inside the limit with minimal oversizing. H=26 gives ≈0.118 mm (still fails).

Cantilever plate (span L=135 mm, width=190 mm): δ ∝ PL³/(3·E_eff·I) with I=190·H³/12 and E_eff=E/(1−ν²)=2508 MPa. Solving gives δ≈2065/H³ mm. At H=23 → 0.170 mm (fails). Critical H where δ=0.11: H=(2065/0.11)^(1/3)≈26.6 mm. H=27 yields ≈0.105 mm, just inside the 0.11 limit with ~5% margin and minimal oversizing.

H0=29mm fails at T=0.088mm. The domain ceiling is 31mm. Displacement scales roughly as 1/H^3 for a plate in bending, so going from 29 to 31mm gives a factor of (29/31)^3 ≈ 0.82 reduction — likely enough to pass. Starting at the maximum avoids wasting solves on intermediate heights that may still fail.

29 mm fails and the allowed domain ceiling is 31 mm. Testing the maximum first confirms whether any solution exists in the domain and, if it passes, gives us a bracket [29, 31] for bisection in a subsequent solve.
H0=29 mm fails. Domain ceiling is 31 mm. With only two candidates left (30 and 31), trying 30 mm first minimises oversizing: if it passes, we stop; if it fails, 31 mm is the only remaining option.
Bisect between 28 (fails) and 31 (upper bound). 30 mm is a reasonable midpoint to quickly narrow the feasible range with one solve.

Binary search start: midpoint between 28 (fails) and 31 (upper bound). Displacement scales roughly as H^-3 for bending stiffness, so going from 28 to 30 gives ~(28/30)^3 ≈ 0.82x displacement reduction. If H0=28 is close to the threshold, 30 mm should suffice without oversizing to 31.
Binary search between 28 (fails) and 31 (upper bound). Starting at 30 mm as a first probe to narrow the range efficiently.
H0=27 fails; domain is [27,31]. Binary search midpoint of [27,31] is 29. This splits the remaining range efficiently to converge in ~2 more solves.
Binary search in the feasible domain [27, 31] mm. H0=27 fails; upper bound 31 is assumed to pass. Midpoint 29 mm splits the interval efficiently — one solve determines which half to pursue next.
Binary search in [27, 31]: H0=27 fails, upper bound=31. Mid-point is 29 mm — minimises oversizing while halving the search space in one solve.

No FEA data yet. Displacement scales roughly as 1/H^3 for a plate in bending. At H0=25 mm the tray fails T=0.1 mm. To comfortably meet the target while staying within [20,31] mm and leaving room for a binary-search refinement, start near the top of the domain at 30 mm.

No FEA data yet. Displacement scales roughly as H^-3 for bending stiffness. At H0=25 mm the tray fails T=0.1 mm. To meet a tight 0.1 mm limit I need meaningful stiffness gain; H=30 mm gives (25/30)^3 ≈ 0.58 reduction in displacement — a strong first probe near the upper bound to establish feasibility before bisecting downward.

No FEA data yet. Displacement scales roughly as H^-3 for bending stiffness. At H0=25mm we fail T=0.1mm. To meet the requirement with margin while staying in [20,31], start at H=30mm — near the stiff end of the domain to likely satisfy the constraint in one solve, minimizing total solves.
No FEA data yet. Binary search in [23, 31]: midpoint is 27 mm. This splits the feasible range efficiently and avoids oversizing.
Binary search between 27 mm (FAIL) and 31 mm (upper bound). Midpoint is 29 mm.
Binary search in [24, 31] (23 fails). Midpoint is 27.5, rounded up to 28 mm to bias toward passing on first try.
Binary search in [23, 31]: H0=23 fails, upper bound 31 likely passes. Midpoint 27 mm splits the domain efficiently to converge in ~2 more solves.
Binary search between 27 mm (fail) and 31 mm (upper bound). Trying 29 mm as midpoint to converge efficiently.

No FEA data yet. H0=29 mm fails. Domain ceiling is 31 mm. Probing the maximum first confirms whether the requirement is achievable at all. If H=31 passes, bisect between 29 and 31 to find the minimal height. If H=31 fails, the requirement cannot be met in [20,31]. Sensitivity of -0.008 mm/mm is too small to extrapolate reliably without a known baseline displacement.

H0=29 mm fails. Sensitivity is measured at H=30 mm (-0.008018 mm/mm). Probing at 30 mm gives a displacement co-located with the sensitivity, letting me apply a one-step linear correction toward T=0.088 mm in the next solve if needed. Most information-efficient first point.

Using the 1/H³ plate stiffness model calibrated on the local sensitivity at 30 mm (−0.008018 mm/mm): C = sensitivity × H⁴ / 3 ≈ 2165, giving disp(30) ≈ 0.0802 mm < 0.088 mm and disp(29) ≈ 0.0888 mm > 0.088 mm. H=30 is the minimum integer height within [20,31] predicted to satisfy the requirement with no oversizing beyond 1 mm above H0.

Using the 1/H^3 beam scaling law: sensitivity at H=30 is -0.008018 mm/mm → δ(30) ≈ 0.008018×30/3 ≈ 0.0802 mm. Linear extrapolation gives δ(29) ≈ 0.0802 + 0.008018 ≈ 0.0882 mm < 0.092 mm (passes), and δ(28) ≈ 0.0962 mm (fails, consistent). H=29 mm is the minimal integer step above H0 expected to satisfy T=0.092 mm.

At H=29 displacement is 0.09388 mm, excess = 0.00188 mm. Local sensitivity at H=30 is -0.008018 mm/mm, so ΔH ≈ 0.00188/0.008018 ≈ 0.23 mm above 29. H=29.23 rounds to 30 mm — smallest integer that should clear the 0.092 mm threshold.

Sensitivity at H=30 mm is -0.008018 mm/mm. Plate-bending scaling gives disp(30)≈0.080 mm < 0.092 mm target; linear back-extrapolation to H=28 adds +0.016 mm, consistent with H0 failing. Response is steeper below 30 mm, so H=30 is the reliable anchor. It keeps overshoot minimal while confirming the measurement reference point.

H0=28 mm fails. The sensitivity edge is measured at H=30 mm, making that point the most reliable for estimation. Starting at 30 mm uses the oracle's own neighbourhood, avoids oversizing toward 31 mm, and gives a verified displacement to anchor any subsequent binary search within [30, 31] if needed.

No FEA data yet. Sensitivity is measured at H=30 mm, making it the best-informed first probe. H0=27 fails; H=30 adds 3 mm of bending stiffness (~×1.37 via H³) and sits where the local gradient −0.008 mm/mm is valid. Pass → back off toward 28–29 to reduce oversizing. Fail → H=31 is the only remaining option.

Sensitivity at H=30: dδ/dH=-0.008018 → δ(30)≈0.080 mm (below 0.095). 1/H³ crossover is near 28.4 mm. H=29 sits just above, accounting for steeper response below H=30, minimising oversizing. One more step to H=30 closes the loop if it fails.

Using u(h) ~ C/h³ with the local sensitivity d(u)/dh = -0.008018 at h=30 gives C = 0.008018 × 30⁴/3 ≈ 2165, hence u(30) ≈ 0.080 mm and u(27) ≈ 0.110 mm (consistent with the fail). The threshold crossing is near h ≈ (C/T)^(1/3) = (2165/0.095)^(1/3) ≈ 28.4 mm. Proposing 29 mm provides a one-step margin above the predicted crossing while avoiding oversizing beyond 30 mm.

Cubic model (disp∝H^-3) calibrated via local sensitivity at 30 mm: -0.008018≈-3·disp(30)/30 → disp(30)≈0.080 mm. Back-project to H=25: 0.080·(30/25)^3≈0.138 mm. Crossover: 0.1=0.138·(25/H)^3 → H≈27.9 mm. +1 mm margin for steeper true response far from 30 mm neighbourhood → 29 mm.

Local sensitivity at H=30: dδ/dH=−0.008018 → δ(30)≈0.080 mm. Cubic scaling δ∝H^−3 gives δ(29)≈0.089 mm < T=0.1 mm, δ(28)≈0.098 mm too close to limit. H=29 gives confidence margin without oversizing to 30.

Using the sensitivity -0.008018 mm/mm at h=30 with 1/h³ cantilever scaling: d(δ)/d(h) = -3δ/h gives δ(30) ≈ 0.008018×30/3 ≈ 0.080 mm. Extrapolating to the threshold 0.1 mm: h = 30×(0.080/0.100)^(1/3) ≈ 27.8 mm. Rounding up to 28 mm targets the constraint boundary with minimal oversizing.

At H=28 displacement=0.1036mm, need -0.0036mm. Sensitivity at H=30 is -0.008018 mm/mm; scaled to H=28 via (30/28)^4 gives ~-0.0105 mm/mm. Required ΔH≈0.34mm → H≈28.34mm. Rounding to 29mm adds a small margin against nonlinearity without oversizing, staying well inside [20,31].

Using the local sensitivity dD/dh = -0.008018 mm/mm at h=30 mm and the bending-stiffness scaling D ∝ 1/h³, I back-calculated D(30) ≈ 0.080 mm. Solving 0.080*(30/h)³ = 0.11 gives h ≈ 27 mm. This is the predicted compliance threshold; a single solve here will either confirm satisfaction or bound the remaining search to [27, 30].

At H=27 the displacement is 0.1153 mm, 0.005 mm above the 0.11 mm limit. Using a plate-bending scaling d(disp)/dH ≈ -3·disp/H ≈ -0.0128 mm/mm at H=27, a +1 mm step yields an estimated displacement of ~0.102 mm, comfortably below 0.11 mm with minimal oversizing. H=28 mm is the smallest integer step likely to clear the requirement.

Using plate bending theory (displacement ∝ 1/H³) with the local sensitivity d(disp)/dH = -0.008018 mm/mm at H=30 mm: d(30) ≈ 0.008018×30/3 = 0.0802 mm. Inverting the power law gives the threshold H = 30×(0.0802/0.11)^(1/3) ≈ 27.0 mm. H=28 mm sits just above this estimate, likely satisfying the ≤0.11 mm requirement with minimal oversizing and one solve.

Using the local sensitivity at 30 mm (-0.008018 mm/mm) and assuming d ~ 1/H^3, back-solving gives C ≈ 2165, d(30) ≈ 0.080 mm and d(23) ≈ 0.178 mm (consistent with failure). The crossing d(H)=0.11 mm solves to H ≈ 27.0 mm. A +1 mm margin to 28 mm guards against the stated steeper true response away from 30 mm, while keeping oversizing minimal and well within [20,31].
